author: Derrick Mitchell
title: Champaign City Council rejects special use permit for commissary kitchen - NewsBreak
text:
By Derrick Mitchell ,
2 hours ago
CHAMPAIGN, Ill. (WCIA) -- Mixed emotions were felt across Champaign Wednesday after the city council voted against a commissary kitchen.
This space would allow chefs to prepare their food in an industrial kitchen and then transport those items to their food trucks or to catering events to sell.
U of I’s YMCA collecting donations for annual Dump and Run event They needed six "yes" votes for this space to become a reality, but during the city council meeting Tuesday night, only four people voted to approve it, while three people voted against it.
Both the applicant and officials from the city said Champaign needs a commissary kitchen -- but those opposing the measure said it needs to go in a different location than what was proposed.
Jeff Marino, a planning manager with the City of Champaign, said one of the reasons the council voted against bringing a commissary kitchen to the community was because neighbors "expressed concern about noise and vehicular traffic and smells."
"The three no votes, I would imagine, were related to the public testimony where they, the neighbors, had expressed some concern about the negative impacts on their neighborhoods," Marino said.
It was proposed to go near Church and Wright Streets in Champaign, not far from OSF.
Champaign Co. Sheriff’s Office prepares to send off retired, senior K-9 with final ride Marino said the zoning of this location made a difference in the decision.
"The proposal was for a commissary kitchen in an MF2 medium density multifamily residential zoning district. So, the commissary kitchen wouldn't normally be allowed there," he explained.
Luis Salgado, an area chef, proposed the special permit and he said it's a way to help small businesses thrive. It's something Marino agrees with.
"The city is 100% in support of small, locally owned businesses and investment that will help those businesses thrive and prosper. In this particular example, it was a case of, was this the right location for it? And because it was surrounded by single family homes, I think the council had some concerns about the impact on those homes," Marino said.
Marino said there is another way for the kitchen to come to Champaign, that could be a win-win for everyone.
Champaign Co. Sheriff releases results of July speed enforcement details "He absolutely could start right away and, probably be, you know, have some success and prosper. But yeah, unfortunately, because of this location, because it was zoned residential, it made it a little more difficult to use it for that land use," Marino said.
Next steps include waiting one year before applying again. WCIA spoke who Salgado, who sent the following statement:
Our goal was to bring more business opportunities to the neighborhood. We worked hard to purchase a vacant lot and improved it.
Salgado He is now working to figure out a different location to propose next time.
